subject: Harmonized commit swing plan: multi-year ramp + co-term options
messages:
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-industries.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-industries.com
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning renewal structure — multi-year ramp + co-term question

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're nearing the internal renewal window and want to explore a structure that gives us headroom for growth without front-loading spend. High level: Acme wants a two-to-three year commitment that ramps capacity over time, and we'd like to align (co-term) this contract with our existing analytics stack renewal in Jan so billing is simpler.

Can you share the types of ramp structures you can support (quarterly unlocks, staged credits, acceleration credits) and whether Redwood will allow auto-renew opt-in with a 60-day notice? Also: any standard language around early-exit / true-up? Procurement asked for an initial pricing sketch to circulate.

Appreciate a short options set we can review.

Best,
Sam
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Industries
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-industries.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal structure — multi-year ramp + co-term question

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. I put together three concise options and attached a spreadsheet + a draft SOW: Acme_Commit_Options_v3.xlsx, SOW_draft.pdf. TL;DR below and then recommended next steps.

Option A — Stepped 24m ramp (conservative)
- 12 month base commit (50% of peak) then quarterly unlocks to reach 100% by month 24
- Auto-renew allowed with 60-day opt-out
- Standard true-up at quarter end; early-exit prorated refund less attrition fee

Option B — Accelerated 24m (recommended for aggressive scale)
- 6 month onboarding credit + linear ramp to 100% by month 18, 24m contract term
- 10% onboarding credit applied in first invoice cycle
- Co-term option available to align to Jan 1 (we can pro-rate mid-year)

Option C — Multi-year (36m) with step-down pricing
- Lower unit price but two-year guaranteed minimum then optional year 3 at reduced rate
- Annual true-ups and capped overage rate

Recommendation: Option B gives the best unit economics for Acme while keeping flexibility. If you want co-terming to Jan 1, we can pro-rate the initial partial period and run a 12–18 month fiscal alignment schedule (see tab "Co-term Sync" in the spreadsheet).

Next steps: 1) Tell us preferred option and target co-term date; 2) procurement timeline (PO, security review, legal redlines); 3) we'll produce a formal quote & DocuSign packet.

Notes: I've CC'd Marissa (sales lead) and Karthik (contracts) to surface any commercial/legal constraints.

Cheers,
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-industries.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal structure — multi-year ramp + co-term question

Looping in a quick commercial view from my side.

Sofia — good options. For Acme I can approve:
- A 10% one-time onboarding credit for Option B (first invoice)
- A co-term pro-rate mechanism to move their renewal to Jan 1 (this will create a partial first invoice period)
- A capped overage rate (we'll cap at 1.5x list for the first 6 months post-ramp)

If they commit to a 24m minimum, we can add a mid-term expansion discount trigger at +30% committed capacity, which reduces unit price by 7% on the incremental bucket. This is a standard upsell incentive to avoid manual renegotiation.

Please confirm finance and legal can accept the pro-rate approach and the capped overage. Connor, can you confirm the billing flow (monthly invoices vs. quarterly invoicing + true-up) and whether prepay changes our discount policy?

-Marissa
SVP, ARR & Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-industries.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 08 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal structure — multi-year ramp + co-term question

Thanks — a few operational points from legal/finance perspective:

1) Billing cadence: we prefer quarterly invoices with monthly usage true-up for multi-year commits. If Acme prefers monthly invoicing, we can accommodate but prepay discounts differ.
2) Early-exit language: standard termination for convenience with a 90-day notice + pro-rated refund for unused prepay less a 10% termination administration fee. We can negotiate on large enterprise deals.
3) Co-terming: we will pro-rate the partial period to align to Jan 1. That partial period will be treated as a first invoice run (no onboarding credit applied twice).

Connor — confirm whether the mid-term expansion discount (Marissa suggested) can be automated in billing or if we should implement via a credit note/manual adjustment. Also please flag any SLA/credit implications tied to burst capacity.

Karthik
Head of Contracts & Pricing
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme-industries.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-industries.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Jun 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aligning renewal structure — multi-year ramp + co-term question

Sofia / Marissa — thanks, this is very helpful. Acme would like to move forward with Option B (Accelerated 24m) with the 10% onboarding credit and the mid-term expansion discount trigger. We agree to the co-terming to Jan 1 with the pro-rate as you outlined. Procurement will expect the formal quote and DocuSign packet, plus the SOW showing ramp milestones.

Requested items for the quote:
- Clearly show first partial period pro-rate amount, subsequent quarterly cadence, and onboarding credit applied on first invoice
- Expansion trigger language (automatic 7% unit discount on incremental bucket at +30% commit)
- Early-exit clause (90-day notice, pro-rate, 10% admin)

We'll aim to have legal review and return redlines within 7 business days. Please send the DocuSign link when the packet is ready.

Best,
Sam
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme Industries
